question: Should OpenClaw permit trusted operators to override the WAL-reset version guard for shared-system SQLite builds whose distro backport cannot be proven from sqlite_version()?
rationale: The runtime cannot infer patch provenance from SQLite 3.46.1, while an unconditional rejection blocks legitimately backported distributions and an assertion-only override can expose persistent state to corruption if misused.

options.title: Strict default plus shared override
options.body: Keep fail-closed behavior and add a strongly warned override limited to demonstrably shared-system SQLite builds, with embedded-build rejection and focused tests.

options.title: Require recognized versions only
options.body: Reject all non-enumerated SQLite versions and resolve this issue only through clearer messaging and documentation directing operators to upgrade the runtime.

options.title: Accept distro versions automatically
options.body: Infer safety from distribution packaging or version ordering, which improves compatibility but cannot reliably prove that the required SQLite patch is present.

recommendation.title: Strict default plus shared override
recommendation.body: Keep fail-closed behavior and add a strongly warned override limited to demonstrably shared-system SQLite builds, with embedded-build rejection and focused tests.
